A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DARKCLUSTERS-15K dataset and physics-guided diffusion reconstruction framework. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched across revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments, quantitative benchmark results in Table 2, uncertainty and input-ablation analyses, and a MACS 1206 reconstruction.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds baseline results, physical reconstruction metrics, revised calibration evidence, and quantitative MACS 1206 comparisons.

M1.justification: The DAPS updates, EDM objective, and lensing losses are retained. Section 5.1 changes the network input from two to four channels, but v1 Section 6.4 already says three photometry bands were used in training. The PDFs do not establish whether this reflects an architectural change or correction of an inconsistent description.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same TNG redshift coverage, SIMBA simulations, and MACS 1206 case. The revised cluster counts include redshift snapshots already described in v1; the 15,000 projections and train/test coverage remain unchanged. The new MACS appendix documents an existing experiment.

E2.justification: Kaiser–Squires inversion becomes an evaluated baseline in Table 2 and Figure 5; v1 only discussed it as prior work. Napier et al., UNet, and the MACS 1206 comparison with Caminha et al. are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds held-out deflection and shear RMSE, observed-versus-expected confidence coverage, and MACS 1206 checks using critical curves at source redshift approximately 1.44, image-position RMS, and enclosed mass within 100 kpc. These extend the evaluation protocol; the stated dataset splits, 100-cluster benchmark evaluation, and DAPS inference settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds fractional-error maps in Figure 5 and a brief DDPM++ versus Diffusion Transformer comparison in Appendix C, reporting comparable performance with higher transformer cost. It also revises the calibration analysis and expands the existing MACS 1206 case study. The input-modality ablation and appendix light–mass correlation analysis remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Figure 3 replaces RMSE-versus-predicted-standard-deviation correlation with a reliability diagram assessing observed versus expected confidence levels on held-out data, substantially changing the calibration assessment. Section 6.4 also newly reports uncertainties for enclosed mass and relative mass error across 20 generated samples. Twenty-sample reconstruction summaries already existed; an increase in sampling runs is not established.

E6.justification: Original Table 2 scores are retained, while Kaiser–Squires results and deflection/shear errors substantially expand the results. The new TNG deflection metric favors UNet over the proposed method: 0.411 versus 0.530 RMSE. MACS 1206 newly has image-position RMS of 0.56 arcseconds versus Caminha et al.'s 0.44, and enclosed mass of (7.61 ± 0.04) × 10^13 solar masses versus (7.25 ± 0.02) × 10^13. These are additional comparisons, not demonstrated improvements over v1 performance.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 removes the explicit identity DLS = DS − DL and instead describes DLS as the lens–source distance. Section 5.2 explicitly states the reduced-shear approximation g = γ/(1 − κ) ≈ γ for κ much smaller than one. These are limited revisions to mathematical definitions and assumptions; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction qualify posterior sampling as approximate and uncertainty calibration as empirical, replacing stronger language about sampling the full posterior. They also clarify that the dataset contains 15,000 mock cluster observations. The principal dataset, automation, speed, and reconstruction contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly interprets the lensing losses as practical data-fidelity terms rather than exact likelihood/noise models, and calibration as evidence of marginal coverage. MACS 1206 is framed as a proof of concept, with its selection justified by absence of external convergence or shear. Appendix C newly argues that prior backbone choice is not a significant performance bottleneck.

D1.justification: New Appendix B documents MACS 1206 mosaic alignment, cropping/resampling, flux conversion, and selection of 55 images from 15 sources. Appendix C newly specifies 137 million parameters, approximately 10 hours of training, and an RTX 4090 GPU. A project-page link supplies code/data access information. These substantially improve documentation, although Table 2 drops its previous explicit WL SNR 0.01 label.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for diffusion posterior sampling, DDPMs, score-based SDEs, regression calibration, and CLASH observations: Chung, Ho, Song, Kuleshov, and Postman et al. It also corrects MARS's regularizer description from cross-entropy to maximum entropy. The overall novelty positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The main section order and much of the prose remain intact. Localized rewrites clarify dataset counting, approximate inference, calibration, and comparisons. A MACS processing appendix is inserted, existing appendices are renumbered, and running author headers and acknowledgements are updated.

P2.justification: Table 2 is transposed and expanded; Figure 3's calibration plot is replaced with different axes and content; Figure 5 gains Kaiser–Squires and fractional-error columns. Figure 6 is substantially rearranged, adds critical-curve comparisons, and changes the convergence display range. These materially revise the presentation of the main evidence.

improvement.justification: v1 supported calibration chiefly through error–uncertainty correlation and real-cluster agreement visually. v2 provides a coverage-based calibration check, quantitative MACS 1206 validation, and additional lensing-space comparisons, while qualifying posterior claims and supplying substantial reproduction details. These changes strengthen support for central claims rather than merely increasing reported performance. Real-data evidence remains limited to one proof-of-concept cluster.
